{
  "summary": "This PR marks all database read, write, erase, and transaction methods in WalletBatch with [[nodiscard]]. All call sites across the wallet are updated to inspect the return values, handle failure conditions, or explicitly cast to void with an explanatory comment when failure is inconsequential. It also refactors passphrase and unlock methods to return util::Expected with structured error information instead of plain booleans.",
  "problem": "Wallet database write and erase failures are frequently ignored across the codebase. When database operations fail, in-memory state can diverge from on-disk storage (such as updating master keys or descriptor keys only in memory), leaving wallets corrupted, desynchronized, or reporting success for operations that never persisted to disk.",
  "evidence": [
    "PR description: 'A common theme in the wallet is that many database write failures are ignored, when they should probably be handled, or at least documented that a failure is being ignored. This PR marks all database functions in WalletBatch as [[nodiscard]] so that a compiler will tell us if a return value is implicitly ignored.'",
    "Commit 14dcad0ff2: 'Wallet passphrase changes currently report success after the master-key write fails. The new passphrase works only in memory while the old passphrase remains on disk.'",
    "Commit a2326cf0cb: 'Descriptor key insertion currently updates the live key map before writing the key record. If the write fails, a retry sees the live-only key and skips persistence while reporting success.'"
  ],
  "dependencies": {
    "depends_on": [
      "#35752"
    ],
    "enables": []
  },
  "scope_notes": "The branch includes commits from prerequisite PR #35752 which implements atomic encryption updates. The diff updates call sites across wallet loading, descriptor management, watch-only export, scanning, RPCs, and Qt UI.",
  "changed_since_previous": "",
  "card": "This pull request marks all database interaction methods in WalletBatch as nodiscard and updates callers across the wallet to handle failures or explicitly document ignored errors. Currently, the wallet ignores many database write failures, causing silent data corruption where live in-memory keys or passphrases diverge from persistent disk records. The author notes that passphrase changes and key insertions previously reported success even after database writes failed. This PR depends on PR 35752 for atomic encryption transaction updates.",
  "needs": [],
  "confidence": "high",
  "uncertainties": []
}

result.card: This pull request marks all database interaction methods in WalletBatch as nodiscard and updates callers across the wallet to handle failures or explicitly document ignored errors. Currently, the wallet ignores many database write failures, causing silent data corruption where live in-memory keys or passphrases diverge from persistent disk records. The author notes that passphrase changes and key insertions previously reported success even after database writes failed. This PR depends on PR 35752 for atomic encryption transaction updates.
